title.narrative: Increasing community access to safe water, sanitation and hygiene to improve income and production

description.narrative: This project is setting out to contributing to CAFOD’s Food and Livelihoods Security and the Emergency Preparedness, Response and Recovery thematic programme frameworks – as set out in the CAFOD Sierra Leone and Liberia Country Strategy Paper (2016-2021). Street Child of Sierra Leone is an implementing Partner for CAFOD, and will be working in collaboration with other partners in Kambia District with requisite expertise in delivering key aspects of the programme. The project will be implemented in communities that were heavily affected by Ebola. The outcomes of this project are in line with the Sierra Leonean Presidents’ Recovery Priorities, which is a 24 month plan that includes Water and Agriculture as key sectors. Kambia District is in the Northern Province, and borders with the Republic of Guinea to the North, Port Loko district to the South and Bombali district to the East. Kambia town is the largest town, and the district capital. There is a diverse district population in Kambia, because of its location and bothering towns with Themnes, Susus in the majority, followed by other ethnic groups such as Madingos, Fullahs and Limbas. The average household size1 is 7 people per family. The livelihood activities of the district residents are mainly farming (rice and roots crops - cassava and yam), followed by cross-border trade with neighboring Guinea. People also engage in fishing and very small scale animal rearing. Men engage in fishing activities, while fish trading in the market is carried out by women. Exchange and hiring of labor is a common practice in the district particularly during the planting and harvest seasons. However, in 2014 this activity drastically dropped compared to pre-Ebola in 2013 and had a significant impact on the seasonal household income. CAFOD has therefore identified Livelihood and Food security support as one of its thematic areas of support in this district, to address the huge post-ebola challenge of reviving the livelihood sector especially in Masungbala Chiefdom, which is one of the most disadvantaged chiefdoms in the district. Emergency Food Security Assessment 2015 findings indicated that the Ebola outbreak has negatively impacted the district population, affecting the vital livelihood activities of crop production (mainly rice). 71 % of the district residents are moderate to severely food insecure.
